chosen_property.label: location
chosen_property.justification: The 'location' property directly relates an event to its place of occurrence, matching the observed signature Event → AdministrativeArea.

candidates.label: deathPlace
candidates.comment: A geographical event relation between a person and the place where they died. Also called: place of demise, passing location, decease location. Examples: "Historical Figure" death place "Dallas, Texas", "Family Member" death place "London, UK". Distinct from birthPlace, which is the place of birth.

candidates.label: location
candidates.comment: A location relation between an action, event, interaction counter, or organization and its physical or virtual place. Also called: situated at, takes place at, found at. Examples: "Conference Event location New York Hilton", "Company Organization location 123 Main St", "Online Meeting location Virtual Conference Room".

candidates.label: sportsEvent
candidates.comment: A specific event relation between an exercise action and the sports event during which it occurred. Also called "event of exercise", "competition event", "athletic event". Examples: "The sprint occurred during the sportsEvent Olympics", "The goal was scored in the sportsEvent World Cup match", "This action took place at a sportsEvent marathon.". Distinct from event, which is a more general event property.

candidates.label: timestamp
candidates.comment: A timestamp relation between an instantaneous event and the specific date and time it occurred. Also called event time, occurrence time, moment of event. Examples: "Concert timestamp 2023-10-27T20:00:00", "Login timestamp 2023-11-01T09:30:15Z", "Photo timestamp 2023-05-15T14:22:00".

candidates.label: event
candidates.comment: An event association relation between an action, organization, or place and an event connected to it. Also called "associated event", "related event", "features event". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' event 'Art Exhibition'", "Place 'Park' event 'Summer Festival'", "Inform action event 'Meeting Reminder'". Distinct from events, which is the plural form.

candidates.label: fromLocation
candidates.comment: A from location relation between an exercise, move, or transfer action and the original place of the object or agent before the action occurred. Also called: origin location, starting point, departure place. Examples: "Package Delivery" from location "Warehouse A", "Person Moving" from location "Old Apartment", "Data Transfer" from location "Server Room 1". Distinct from toLocation, which is the destination after the action.

candidates.label: events
candidates.comment: An events association relation between an organization or place and the events connected to it. Also called "associated events", "related events", "features events". Examples: "Organization 'Museum' events 'Art Exhibition, Lecture Series'", "Place 'Park' events 'Summer Festival, Winter Fair'", "Company 'Tech Solutions' events 'Annual Conference, Product Launch'". Distinct from event, which is the singular form.

candidates.label: source
candidates.comment: A causal relation between an instantaneous event and the thing that initiated or caused it. Also called "originates from", "caused by", "event trigger", "event origin". Examples: "The explosion's source was a gas leak", "The alarm's source was a smoke detector", "The data breach's source was a phishing attack."

candidates.label: subEvents
candidates.comment: A collection of hierarchical relations between a larger event and multiple smaller events that are components or parts of it. Also called "component events", "nested events", "events within event", "parts of event". Examples: "The conference has subEvents multiple presentations", "The festival's subEvents include several concerts and workshops", "This event comprises many subEvents.". Distinct from subEvent, which refers to a single component event.

candidates.label: recordedAt
candidates.comment: A recording location relation between a creative work and the event where it was recorded. Also called recorded during, captured at event. Examples: "A live album was recorded at 'Wembley Stadium Concert'.", "A documentary film was recorded at 'the Amazon Rainforest Expedition'.", "A podcast episode was recorded at 'a conference panel discussion'.". Distinct from recordedIn, which is the inverse relation.

chosen_property.label: endTime
chosen_property.justification: The 'endTime' property aligns with the 'peaked at' relation as it specifies the time an event concludes, matching the observed signature Event → DateTime.

candidates.label: suggestedMaxAge
candidates.comment: A numerical value indicating the maximum recommended age in years for an audience or user. Also called "maximum age", "upper age limit", "age cap". Examples: "The game has suggestedMaxAge 12", "The audience specification includes suggestedMaxAge 65", "This content is suitable up to suggestedMaxAge 18.". Distinct from suggestedAge, which specifies a range, and suggestedMinAge, which specifies only the minimum.

candidates.label: childMaxAge
candidates.comment: A demographic specification for a parent audience, indicating the maximal age of a child. Also called "maximum child age", "upper age limit for child", "child age cap". Examples: "Parent audience for toddlers childMaxAge 3", "Parent audience for teens childMaxAge 17". Distinct from childMinAge, which specifies the minimal age.

candidates.label: requiredMaxAge
candidates.comment: A required maximum age relation between a people audience and the upper age limit for inclusion. Also called max age, age limit. Examples: "A children's event targets a people audience with required max age '12'.", "A youth program has a required max age '25'.", "A senior discount applies to a people audience with required max age '99'."

candidates.label: maxPrice
candidates.comment: A maximum price relation between a price specification and the highest price in a given range. Also called: highest price, upper price limit, ceiling price. Examples: "Premium Tier maxPrice 99.99", "Luxury Car maxPrice 150000", "Concert Ticket maxPrice 250". Distinct from highPrice, which is used for AggregateOffer and refers to the highest price of all offers.

candidates.label: bestRating
candidates.comment: A number or text representing the highest value allowed in a rating system. Also called: maximum rating, top score, highest possible rating. Examples: "Rating 'Product Review' bestRating '5'", "Rating 'Movie Score' bestRating '10'". Distinct from worstRating, which is the lowest value.

candidates.label: endTime
candidates.comment: An end time relation between an item (such as an action, reservation, or media object) and the time it is expected to conclude or when a clip ends. Also called "conclusion time", "finish time", "closing time". Examples: "Reservation 'Dinner' endTime '20:00'", "Action 'Meeting' endTime '17:00'", "Media clip endTime '00:02:30'". Distinct from endDate, which specifies the end date for longer-term items like events or seasons.

candidates.label: typicalAgeRange
candidates.comment: A typical age range relation between a creative work or event and the expected age group of its audience. Also called age suitability, target age, recommended age. Examples: "Book typicalAgeRange '7-9'", "Movie typicalAgeRange '13+'", "Event typicalAgeRange 'all ages'".

candidates.label: endOffset
candidates.comment: An end offset relation between a clip and the number or HyperTocEntry representing its end time from the beginning of the work. Also called "clip end time", "segment end", "finish offset". Examples: "Video clip endOffset '120' (seconds)", "Audio segment endOffset 'HyperTocEntry for Chapter 5'", "Media clip endOffset '300'". Distinct from endTime, which is a more general property for the end time of various items, including actions and media objects.

candidates.label: percentile90
candidates.comment: A statistical attribute indicating the 90th percentile value within a quantitative value distribution. Also called 90th percentage point, upper decile. Examples: A distribution has a percentile90 of 90. The data shows a percentile90 of 45.5. The scores have a percentile90 of 95.

candidates.label: aggregateRating
candidates.comment: An aggregate rating relation between an item (e.g., product, service, creative work) and its overall rating derived from multiple reviews. Also called overall score, collective rating, average review. Examples: "A product's aggregate rating is '4.5 stars'.", "A movie's aggregate rating is '8.2/10'."

candidates.label: coverageStartTime

Examples: "Election Night Live Blog" coverage start time "2024-11-05T18:00:00Z", "Sports Event Live Update" coverage start time "2023-07-15T14:00:00Z", "Conference Live Blog" coverage start time "2023-10-27T09:00:00Z". Distinct from coverageEndTime, which indicates when coverage concludes.

candidates.label: geoCovers
candidates.comment: A geo covers relation representing a spatial relationship where one geometry or place completely covers another, meaning every point of the covered entity is within the covering entity. Also called: covers, encompasses, overlies. Examples: "Country 'France'" geo covers "City 'Paris'", "North America" geo covers "Lake 'Superior'", "City 'Springfield'" geo covers "House '123 Main St'". Distinct from geoCoveredBy, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy
candidates.comment: A mission coverage priorities policy relation between a news media organization and a creative work or URL stating its coverage priorities or public agenda. Also called: editorial policy, coverage guidelines, journalistic priorities. Examples: "News Outlet missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Focus on local news and investigative journalism'", "Broadcaster missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Public Service Mandate'", "Digital Publisher missionCoveragePrioritiesPolicy 'Transparency and Accuracy Statement'".

candidates.label: includedInHealthInsurancePlan
candidates.comment: A health insurance plan inclusion relation between a drug and a health insurance plan that covers it. Also called covered by plan, plan coverage, drug coverage. Examples: "A drug is included in a health insurance plan.", "The medication is covered by an included in health insurance plan.", "This drug is part of a specific health insurance plan."

candidates.label: numberOfPartialBathrooms
candidates.comment: The total number of half and quarter bathrooms in an accommodation or floor plan. Also called partial bathroom count, half baths, quarter baths. Examples: "Apartment A numberOfPartialBathrooms 1", "House B numberOfPartialBathrooms 2", "Hotel Room C numberOfPartialBathrooms 0". Distinct from numberOfFullBathrooms, which specifies full or three-quarter bathrooms. numberOfBathroomsTotal is the sum of all types.

candidates.label: area
candidates.comment: An area relation between a broadcast service and the geographic place where its users can access it. Also called service region, coverage area, broadcast zone. Examples: "A radio station's area is 'Greater London'.", "The TV service's area is 'North America'."

candidates.label: variantCover
candidates.comment: A variant cover relation between a comic issue and a description of its variant printing cover. Also called alternative cover, special edition cover, variant description. Examples: "ComicIssue variantCover 'Bryan Hitch Variant Cover'", "ComicIssue variantCover '2nd Printing Variant'", "ComicIssue variantCover 'Sketch Cover Edition'".

candidates.label: benefitsSummaryUrl
candidates.comment: A URL that links directly to the summary of benefits and coverage for a health insurance plan. Also called: summary of benefits link, plan benefits URL. Examples: "HealthInsurancePlan 'Standard Plan A' benefitsSummaryUrl 'http://example.com/planA-benefits.pdf'."

candidates.label: geoCoveredBy
candidates.comment: A geo covered by relation representing a spatial relationship where a geometry or place is entirely covered by another geometry or place. Also called: is covered by, lies within, is contained by. Examples: "City 'Paris'" geo covered by "Country 'France'", "Lake 'Superior'" geo covered by "North America", "House '123 Main St'" geo covered by "City 'Springfield'". Distinct from geoCovers, which is the inverse relation.

candidates.label: founder

Examples: "Microsoft" founder "Bill Gates", "Apple Inc." founder "Steve Jobs", "Google" founder "Larry Page". Distinct from founders, which is specifically for multiple people.

candidates.label: countryOfOrigin

candidates.label: editor

candidates.label: makesOffer

candidates.label: byDay

candidates.label: previousStartDate

candidates.label: broadcaster

chosen_property.label: previousStartDate
chosen_property.justification: The 'previousStartDate' property directly relates an event to a previous date, matching the observed signature Event → DateTime.

candidates.label: successorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a newer product model and its previous, often discontinued, predecessor. Also called "replaces", "evolved from", "preceded by", "derived from". Examples: "iPhone 15 is successorOf iPhone 14", "The new car model is successorOf the previous generation", "This product is a successorOf an older variant."

candidates.label: previousItem
candidates.comment: A sequential relation between a list item and the list item that immediately precedes it. Also called precedes, comes after, follows. Examples: List item 'B' has a previous item 'A'. The current item's previous item is the one before it. In a breadcrumb trail, the current page has a previous item. Distinct from nextItem, which links to the item that follows.

candidates.label: supersededBy
candidates.comment: A deprecation relation between an older term (property, class, or enumeration) and a newer term that replaces or supersedes it. Also called "replaced by", "obsoleted by", "succeeded by", "deprecated by". Examples: "OldProperty is supersededBy NewProperty", "The deprecated class is supersededBy a modern equivalent", "This enumeration value is supersededBy a more precise one."

candidates.label: nextItem
candidates.comment: A list item that immediately follows the current list item in an ordered sequence. Also called subsequent item, following item, next in list. Examples: "Item 1 nextItem 'Item 2'", "Page 3 nextItem 'Page 4'", "Step A nextItem 'Step B'". Distinct from previousItem, which links to the preceding item.

candidates.label: predecessorOf
candidates.comment: A lineage relation between a product model and its newer, often superseding, variant. Also called replaced by, succeeded by, updated to, newer version is. Examples: iPhone 10 is a predecessor of iPhone 11. Model A is a predecessor of Model B. The old software version is a predecessor of the new one. Distinct from successorOf, which points from a newer variant to an older one.

candidates.label: honorificPrefix
candidates.comment: An honorific prefix relation between a person and a title preceding their name. Also called title, salutation, courtesy title. Examples: "A person has an honorific prefix 'Dr.'.", "Her honorific prefix is 'Ms.'.", "The individual uses the honorific prefix 'Mr.'."

candidates.label: beforeMedia
candidates.comment: A media object representing the circumstances prior to performing a how-to direction. Also called: pre-action media, initial state media. Examples: "HowToDirection 'Install Shelf' beforeMedia 'Image of empty wall'", "HowToDirection 'Bake Cake' beforeMedia 'Video of ingredients on counter'."

candidates.label: tocContinuation
candidates.comment: A table of contents continuation relation between a HyperToc entry and the next default HyperToc entry to play or render. Also called next entry, subsequent entry, continued by. Examples: "Chapter 1 tocContinuation 'Chapter 2'", "Segment A tocContinuation 'Segment B'", "HyperTocEntry 'Intro' tocContinuation 'Main Content'".

candidates.label: recognizedBy
candidates.comment: A recognition relation between a credential and the organization that acknowledges its validity or value. Also called accredited by, validated by, acknowledged by. Examples: "A university degree is recognized by 'the Ministry of Education'.", "A professional certification is recognized by 'an industry association'.", "A medical license is recognized by 'the Medical Board'."

candidates.label: datePublished

Examples: "Book" date published "1984-06-08", "TV Show Episode" date published "2023-01-01", "Certification" date published "2022-12-01". Distinct from dateCreated, which is the date of creation, and datePosted, which is for online listings.

Examples: "A product has a measurement for its height.", "An offer includes a measurement for package weight.", "The certification has a measurement of carbon footprint."

candidates.label: wheelbase

Also called wheel distance, axle distance, inter-axle distance. Examples: Sedan wheelbase 2.7 meters, Motorcycle wheelbase 1.5 meters, SUV wheelbase 3.0 meters.

candidates.label: measurementDenominator
candidates.comment: A measurement denominator relation between an observation or statistical variable and the variable used as the denominator in a ratio or percentage. Also called: ratio denominator, base variable, reference variable. Examples: "Unemployment Rate Observation measurementDenominator 'Total Labor Force'", "Per Capita Income StatisticalVariable measurementDenominator 'Population'", "Percentage Change Observation measurementDenominator 'Initial Value'".

candidates.label: measurementQualifier
candidates.comment: A measurement qualifier relation between an observation or statistical variable and an enumeration providing additional qualification. Also called: observation qualifier, measurement attribute, data context. Examples: "GDP Observation measurementQualifier 'Nominal'", "Inflation Rate measurementQualifier 'Annualized'", "Population Count measurementQualifier 'Estimated'".

candidates.label: measurementMethod
candidates.comment: A measurement method relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the specific method used for measurement. Also called: method of measurement, specific technique, measurement approach. Examples: "Temperature Dataset measurementMethod 'Thermocouple'", "Survey Data measurementMethod 'Likert Scale'", "Chemical Analysis measurementMethod 'Spectrophotometry'". Distinct from measurementTechnique, which is a broader property that measurementMethod is a subproperty of.

candidates.label: valueReference

Also called reference value, contextual value, measurement context. Examples: "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'Standard Temperature'", "PropertyValue valueReference 'Color Spectrum'", "QuantitativeValue valueReference 'RPM at max torque'".

candidates.label: measurementTechnique
candidates.comment: A measurement technique relation between a data catalog, data download, dataset, observation, property value, or statistical variable and the technique, method, or technology used for measurement. Also called: measurement approach, data collection method, analytical technique. Examples: "Molecule Concentration Dataset measurementTechnique 'Mass Spectrometry'", "Depression Rating Observation measurementTechnique 'Beck Depression Inventory'", "Water Quality Data measurementTechnique 'Chromatography'". Distinct from measurementMethod, which is a more specific subproperty.

candidates.label: lesserOrEqual
candidates.comment: A lesser or equal ordering relation between two qualitative values, indicating that the subject value is smaller than or equal to the object value. Also called: is less than or equal to, is at most, does not exceed. Examples: "Low lesserOrEqual Medium", "Small lesserOrEqual Small", "Cold lesserOrEqual Cold". Distinct from lesser, which strictly indicates a smaller value.

candidates.label: measuredProperty

candidates.label: width
